RAINFALL Act I · Canopy
Rainfall striking broadleaf canopy

Rainfall

a study in what still works

Held together by hand

Wet silt tamped by palm along the lower ridge before the overflow cuts through the rootbed.

WATER

Precipitation collects petroleum sheen from curbs and concrete channels, unable to reach an aquifer.

AIR

Falling rain scrubs airborne nitrates and sulfuric exhaust, lowering rainwater pH before it hits the roofline.

LAND

Parched, compacted soil repels moisture; toxic runoff carves hard gullies through dead root matter.

Rain falls the same everywhere. What it meets decides what it becomes.

Documenting the hydrologic cycle through three stages of contact: intact canopy absorption, agrarian stewardship, and industrial runoff saturation.
